newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen selling 10-yrs under-the-table -- traders.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen selling 10-yrs under-the-table -- traders.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Reserve is seen selling the middle part of the yield curve on behalf of some foreign central banks, money market sources said.
"We heard talk of the Fed selling under-the-table," said a trader at a U.S. investment bank. "There was talk of some big middle-East sellers, mainly on 10-year notes," he added.

A spokesman for the Federal Reserve Bank of New York said the central bank would not comment on the rumor. "We've decided not to comment on anything that isn't an open market operation," the spokesman said.
Market players cited rumors of a large hedge fund selling five-year notes as weighing on prices as well.
The 6-3/4 percent 30-year benchmark Treasury bond, which traded up as much as 3/4 of a point earlier in the day, was quoted off 10/32 at 101-1/32 in late morning trade.
Its yield was at 6.66 percent, well above the day's lows at 6.59 percent.
